Rashi on Chagigah 4b:10:1.hebrew: כולי האי ואולי - כל היסורין הללו יקבל, ועודנו בספק אם תהיה לו תקוה:
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:10:1.english: All this, and “perhaps”? - He will accept all these sufferings, and he is still in doubt whether he will have hope.

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:11:1.hebrew: ויש נספה בלא משפט - יש אדם כלה, ואין עון בידו, ולא היה משפט לספות:
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:11:1.english: And there is one swept away without justice - There is one who perishes though there is no sin in his hand, and there was no judgment [warranting] sweeping [him] away.

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:11:2.hebrew: ומי איכא דאזיל כו' - הש"ס קא בעי לה:
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:11:2.english: And is there anyone who goes, etc. - The Talmud is asking this.

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:11:3.hebrew: אמר ליה - אמר מלאך המות לשלוחו:
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:11:3.english: He said to him - The angel [of death] said to his agent.

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:11:4.hebrew: אייתי לי מרים מגדלא נשייא - הרוג את מרים המקלעת שיער הנשים:
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:11:4.english: Bring me Miriam the women's hairdresser - Kill Miriam, who braids women's hair.

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:12:1.hebrew: היכי יכלת לה - מאחר שלא הגיע זמנה:
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:12:1.english: How were you able [to take] her? - Since her time had not yet arrived.

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:12:2.hebrew: הות נקיטא מתארא בידה - היתה אוחזת בידה האוד של תנור, והוא שקורין פרגו"ן:
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:12:2.english: She was holding a shovel in her hand - She was holding in her hand the poker of an oven, which is called in Old French pergon:

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:1:1.hebrew: מפנקי - שאין הולכין בלא מנעל, דאין אדם נכנס להר הבית במנעלו, דכתיב: "מי בקש זאת מידכם רמוס חצרי":
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:1:1.english: Delicate ones - Who cannot walk without a shoe, for a person may not enter the Temple Mount with their shoe, as it is written: "Who has required this at your hand, to trample My courts?"

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:2:1.english: Exempt from appearance - They are not obligated to send their appearance burnt-offerings by means of a messenger.

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:2:2.hebrew: טמא אינו (חייב) בביאה, שאינו יכול ליכנס למקדש, דכתיב (כי מקדש) ה' טמא ונכרתה (במדבר י״ט:י״ג):
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:2:2.english: A ritually impure person is not (obligated) in coming, because he cannot enter the Temple, as it is written: (“For he has defiled the Sanctuary of) the Lord. [That person] who is impure shall be cut off” (Numbers 19:13).

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:3:1.hebrew: ערל - ישראל שמתו אחיו מחמת מילה:
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:3:1.english: Uncircumcised - A Jew whose brothers died on account of circumcision.

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:3:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן - ״אלא ערל מנלן? הא מני רבי עקיבא היא,״ דמרבי ליה ערל כטמא:
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:3:2.english: Thus we read - ["However, the uncircumcised, from where do we derive it? This is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva,"] who includes the uncircumcised like the impure:

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:3:3.hebrew: איש איש - מזרע אהרן, והוא צרוע או זב:
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:3:3.english: "Any man [ish ish]" - of the seed of Aaron, who is a leper or one with a discharge.

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:3:4.hebrew: לרבות את הערל - שהוא כטמא, שלא יאכל תרומה אם כהן הוא:
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:3:4.english: To include the uncircumcised - That he is like the impure person, [so] that he may not eat terumah if he is a priest.

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:6:1.hebrew: עבד - שהוא חביב לרבו, עד שרבו מצפה ושואף מתי יראהו — יתרחק מעליו:
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:6:1.english: A slave - who is so beloved to his master that his master hopes and longs for when he will see him — [can such a slave] be distanced from him?

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:6:2.hebrew: יתרחק מעליו - איך הגיע יום שנהפך לו לשונא, ורחקו, וצוה שלא יראהו? שנאמר: כי תבאו וגו':
Rashi on Chagigah 4b:6:2.english: He will distance himself from him - How could the day arrive that [the master] turns into an enemy to him, and distances him, and commands that he not see him? As it is stated: "When you come [to appear before Me]..."

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:8:1.english: Rebuke - That he rebukes [a person for] his transgression to his face.

Rashi on Chagigah 4b:9:1.english: What is it? - From where do we know that he was afraid?

Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:11:1.hebrew: אמר מי איכא איניש דאזיל בלא זימניה - ל"ג "אמר", שהרי רב יוסף לא היה שואל כך, שעל זה לא מתרץ לו הש"ס כלום; אלא הש"ס קא פריך ליה:
Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:11:1.english: "He said: Is there a person who goes before his time?" - We do not read the word "he said," for Rav Yosef did not ask this, since the Gemara gives him no answer to it; rather, it is the Gemara that is asking [this question] against him:

Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:11:2.hebrew: הוה שכיח גביה מלאך המות - דמספר מה שאירע לו כבר, דהאי עובדא דמרים מגדלא נשייא בבית שני היה, דהיתה אמו של פלוני, כדאיתא בשבת (דף קד: ושם):
Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:11:2.english: “The Angel of Death was frequently with him” - For [the Angel of Death] was relating something that had already happened to him [i.e., in the past], since this incident of Miriam the women's hair-braider occurred in the time of the Second Temple, for she was the mother of a certain person, as it is stated in Shabbat (104b and there):

Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:1:1.hebrew: כי תבואו לראות פני - פירש רש"י: דנפקא ליה מדכתיב "רמוס חצרי", דמשמע דהולך במנעליו. ותימה הוא, דבפרק הרואה (ברכות דף סב:) מפיק ליה מדכתיב "של נעלך". ויש לומר דהתם עיקר, אבל הכא ניחא ליה לאתויי ראייה כדכתיב "כי תבאו לראות" וכו':
Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:1:1.english: "When you come to appear before Me" - Rashi explained that [the exemption] is derived from that which is written "to trample My courts," which implies that one walks in his shoes. And this is puzzling, for in the chapter Haro'eh (Berakhot 62b) he derives it from that which is written "your shoe." And one can say that there [the verse of "your shoe"] is the primary [source], but here it is convenient for him to bring a proof [from the verse] as it is written, "When you come to appear," etc.:

Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:2:1.hebrew: דכתיב ובאת שמה והבאתם שמה - והא דאמרינן (פסחים דף סב.): ערל וטמא משלחין קרבנותיהן, דאע"ג דליתנהו בביאה — התם מיירי בנדרים ונדבות, שאין קבועין זמן בהבאת רגלים, והאי קרא לא משתעי אלא בעולת ראייה, דבעינן ביאה. אך קשה לרבי שמעון, דאמר פרק בתרא דמו"ק (דף טז. ושם): "וביום באו יקריב" (יחזקאל מ״ד:כ״ז) — בזמן שהוא ראוי לביאה יקריב, בזמן שאינו ראוי לביאה לא יקריב. ופשיט מהתם דמצורע לא ישלח קרבנותיו. וכי לית ליה ההוא דלעיל דערל וטמא, דמשמע דליכא מאן דפליג? ולא מסתבר לחלק, דהתם במצורע לחוד, וההיא בשאר טמאים, דהאי קרא בסתמא כתיב, משמע דאכל טמאים קאי. וכי תימא משום דכתיב לעיל מינה "שבעת ימים יספרו לו" (שם), דמשמע בימי סיפורו, דקאי דוקא אמצורע — הא אפסקיה למילתיה: "וביום באו אל הקודש אל החצר הפנימית", דדרשינן מיניה זו עשירית האיפה. ועוד, התם הוה ליה לאתויי לההוא ערל וטמא למיפשט מינה דמשלח שפיר. ונראה בעיני דהתם בקרבנות מצורע מצרעתו מיירי, ובשמיני לרפואה; כי בעי לאתויי קרבנותיו חזר ונצטרע, הלכך האי קרבן דמחוייב לא מצי מייתי, כיון דלאו בר ביאה הוא. אבל בנדרים ונדבות מביא שפיר, אף מצורע כמו שאר טמאים. והתם הארכתי בדבר לפרש מההיא דערל וטמא משלחין קרבנותיהן ולא בעינן סמיכה, כמו בההיא דהשולח חטאתו ממדינת הים דכל הגט (גיטין דף כח: ושם), דפריך לה: והא בעי סמיכה? ומוקי לה בקרבן נשים או בחטאת העוף. דהתם בערל שמתו אחיו מחמת מילה, וטמא כמו מצורע או זב, דאין טהרתו תלויה רק ברפואה, ואפשר שלא יתרפא לעולם, והוה ליה מחוייב קרבן, הלכך טוב לנו שיביא בלא סמיכה. אבל התם בגיטין יש לנו להמתין עד שיביא. עוד הארכתי התם בפרק ג' דגיטין (שם):
Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:2:1.english: “As it is written: ‘And there you shall come’ ‘and there you shall bring’” - And as for that which we say (Pesachim 62a): An uncircumcised person and a ritually impure person may send their offerings — [this is so] even though they are not included in [the mitzva of] coming — there it is speaking of vows and voluntary offerings, which have no fixed time at the pilgrimage festivals, whereas this verse speaks only of the burnt-offering of appearance, for which coming is required. But this is difficult according to Rabbi Shimon, who said in the last chapter of Moed Katan (16a, and there): “And on the day that he comes … he shall offer” (Ezekiel 44:27) — when he is fit to enter, he may offer; when he is not fit to enter, he may not offer. And [the Gemara] derives from there that a leper may not send his offerings. So does he not hold [like] that earlier [teaching] about an uncircumcised and an impure person, which implies that no one disagrees? And it is not reasonable to distinguish, [saying] that there it is about a leper alone, while that [teaching] is about other impure people, for this verse is written without specification, implying that it refers to all impure people. And if you say [that it refers only to a leper] because it is written before it, “Seven days they shall count for him” (there), which implies [that it refers to] the days of his counting, so that it refers specifically to a leper — [but] he interrupted his subject: “And on the day that he comes into the sanctuary, into the inner court,” from which we derive [the law of] the tenth of an ephah. Furthermore, there [in Moed Katan] it should have brought that [teaching about] an uncircumcised and an impure person, to derive from it that he may indeed send. And it appears to me that there it speaks of the offerings of a leper from his leprosy, [brought] on the eighth day for [his] healing; when he wishes to bring his offerings, he has again become leprous. Therefore he cannot bring this offering that is obligatory, since he is not fit to enter. But with vows and voluntary offerings he may indeed bring, even a leper, like other impure people. And there I elaborated on the matter, to explain that [teaching] of “an uncircumcised and an impure person may send their offerings,” and we do not require semikha (laying on of hands), as in that case of one who sends his sin-offering from overseas, in [the chapter] Kol HaGet (Gittin 28b, and there), where [the Gemara] asks: But it requires semikha? And it establishes it as [referring to] the offering of women or the bird sin-offering. For there it is about an uncircumcised person whose brothers died because of circumcision, and an impure person like a leper or a zav, whose purification depends only on healing, and it is possible that he will never be healed, so that he is obligated in an offering; therefore it is good for us that he bring it without semikha. But there in Gittin we can wait until he brings. I elaborated further there in the third chapter of Gittin (there):

Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:3:1.hebrew: דמרבה ערל כי טמא - אמר הרב ר' אלחנן: דהא דאיצטריך קרא דלעיל למעוטי ליה טומטום ואנדרוגינוס, ולא למעוטי מספק ערל — התם אליבא דרבנן הוא, דלרבי עקיבא לא צריך. ומיהו אך קשה: אמאי איצטריך מיעוט לערל גבי פסח? תיפוק ליה מטמא! וי"ל דהתם ממעטינן ערל שמתו אחיו מחמת מילה, דלאו כטמא. ומיהו זהו דוקא לפרש"י, דמפרש התם ערל שמתו אחיו מחמת מילה, יש להעמיד הכי. אבל לפר"ת, דמפרש שדואג מחמת הצער, אבל מתו אחיו מחמת מילה הוי אנוס — יש להקשות לרבי עקיבא דמרבה ערל כי טמא: אמאי איצטריך קרא לערל דפסח? תיפוק ליה מטמא! ויש לומר: דמהתם ידעינן ליה בעלמא; כיון דמדמה ערל לטמא בפסח, דרשינן נמי מ"איש איש" לרבות ערל כטמא. אבל ליכא למימר דאי ליכא קרא אלא דערל כטמא, הייתי אומר דפסח בא בערלות, דאי הוה רובן ערלים כמו בטומאה. דהא מנא ידעינן לרבות ערל כי טמא מ"איש איש"? "כי יהיה צרוע או זב", והתם לא כתיב רק טומאת צרעת וזיבות, ואנן אמרינן בריש "אלו דברים" (פסחים דף סז.) דלא דחי רק טומאת מת בלבד. והשתא סוגיא דהכא פליגא ארבא דריש "הערל" (יבמות דף עב:), דקאמר דלא לישתמיט תנא דמרבה ערל כי טמא, ונוקמא כרבי עקיבא; ופריך ליה מהכא, דערל וטמא פטורין מן הראייה, ומשני: שאני התם משום דמאיס. ומשמע דאפילו רבנן מודו — כלומר, לאו משום דמרבה ליה כי טמא, אלא משום דמאיס. ומיהו י"ל דה"פ: שאני התם משום דמאיס, להכי מרבה ערל כי טמא אליבא דרבי עקיבא, אבל לא שיהא ערל מטמא בנגיעה כטמא, להכי לא תנינהו גבי הדדי:
Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:3:1.english: "Who amplifies the uncircumcised like the impure" - The Rav, Rabbi Elchanan, said: The fact that the verse above was needed to exclude a tumtum and an androginos, and not to exclude the uncircumcised on account of doubt — there [it is stated] according to the Rabbis, since according to Rabbi Akiva it is not needed. But yet it is difficult: Why was an exclusion needed for the uncircumcised with regard to the Paschal offering? Let it be derived from [the case of] the impure! And one can say that there we exclude an uncircumcised person whose brothers died on account of circumcision, who is not like the impure. However, this [answer] applies only according to Rashi, who explains there that [the exclusion refers to] an uncircumcised person whose brothers died on account of circumcision, so that one can establish it this way. But according to Rabbeinu Tam, who explains that he is afraid because of the pain, but if his brothers died on account of circumcision he is under duress — one can ask according to Rabbi Akiva, who amplifies the uncircumcised like the impure: Why was a verse needed for the uncircumcised regarding the Paschal offering? Let it be derived from [the case of] the impure! And one can say: from there [the Paschal offering] we know it generally; since it likens the uncircumcised to the impure regarding the Paschal offering, we also derive from "ish ish" to amplify the uncircumcised like the impure. But one cannot say that if there were no verse except [the one stating] that the uncircumcised is like the impure, I would have said that the Paschal offering is brought in a state of uncircumcision, if most of them were uncircumcised, as with impurity. For from where do we know to amplify the uncircumcised like the impure from "ish ish"? [The verse states] "if he is a leper or has an issue," and there only the impurity of leprosy and of issues is written, whereas we say at the beginning of [the chapter] "Eilu Devarim" (Pesachim 67a) that [the Paschal offering] overrides only the impurity of a corpse alone. And now, the passage here disagrees with Rava in [the chapter] "Ha'Arel" (Yevamot 72b), who said that no Tanna would fail to amplify the uncircumcised like the impure, and let us establish [the Mishnah] according to Rabbi Akiva; and he challenges it from here, [from the fact] that the uncircumcised and the impure are exempt from appearing [at the Temple], and answers: There it is different because he is repulsive. And it implies that even the Rabbis agree — meaning, [the exemption is] not because he amplifies him like the impure, but because he is repulsive. But one can say that this is what [the answer] means: There it is different because he is repulsive, and therefore Rabbi Akiva amplifies the uncircumcised like the impure; but not that the uncircumcised conveys impurity by touch like the impure, and therefore they did not teach them together:

Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:8:1.hebrew: של הקדוש ברוך הוא על אחת כמה וכמה - שלא יוכל להשיב תשובה מעלייתא להיפטר לגמרי, דמכמה דברים מצי לפטור עצמו קצת, כדאיתא בפרק הדר (עירובין דף סה.): יכולני לפטור כל העולם מדין של תפלה:
Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:8:1.english: “[The rebuke] of the Holy One, Blessed be He, all the more so” - [This is] because one will not be able to give a fine answer so as to be completely exempted; for in many matters one can exempt oneself partially, as stated in the chapter Hadar (Eruvin 65a): “I can exempt the entire world from the judgment [that comes] because of prayer.”

Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:9:1.hebrew: דליכא מילתא דכתיב באורייתא דלא קיימתיה - לא בעי למימר שיעיד לו שקיים הכל, דמנא ידע? והא לא היה בדורו! אלא היה אומר: כך וכך דרשתי ועשיתי מעשה, בוא והעידני שכן למדת גם אתה:
Tosafot on Chagigah 4b:9:1.english: "That there is nothing written in the Torah that I did not fulfill" - [Samuel] did not mean to say that [Moses] should testify for him that he fulfilled everything, for how would [Moses] know? He was not in his generation! Rather, [Samuel] was saying: "Thus and so I expounded, and I performed [such] an action; come and testify for me that you too taught it so."
